Away supporters travelling to the SMH Group Stadium can generally expect a positive matchday experience, with many fans praising the friendly atmosphere and welcoming feel around Chesterfield’s home ground. As shown on the stadium seating plan, available on the club’s official website and further down this page, away supporters are usually housed in Block E1 of the Little East Stand. For fixtures with greater demand, Chesterfield can also make Blocks E2 and E3 available, increasing the overall away allocation. The Little East Stand offers an excellent, unobstructed view of the pitch, with no supporting pillars restricting sightlines. Positioned close to the playing surface, travelling supporters are also able to enjoy the atmosphere from one of the nearest vantage points in the stadium. The acoustics in the away end are also brilliant, thanks to the low roof that overhangs the Chesterfield College Community East Stand. This means that away fans can usually be heard loud and clear during matches at the SMH Group Stadium. Food on offer from the concourse includes pies and sausage rolls, while alcohol is also served before kick-off and at half-time. SMH Group Stadium in the news Chesterfield’s ‘Project 9,000’ pushed by club chairman, Ashley Kirk Chesterfield have a passionate local fanbase, but in order for the club to grow on the pitch, they are pushing for more support off of it. The goal of Project 9,000 is to regularly get 9,000 fans through the turnstiles at the SMH Group Stadium for Chesterfield’s home games, and while that seems like a distant dream, the Spireites’ chairman Ashley Kirk continues to work towards it. Speaking at a recent fans’ forum about ways to encourage more supporters to attend matches, Kirk said: “Who wants to see a full stadium at every home game? We are going to get that by people being an ambassador for the club. “Whether it’s society or whether it’s me, I hear a few angry voices saying ‘the recruitment’s rubbish, this is bad, that is bad, sack him,’ and they are the ones that everyone seems to talk about and talk to. “Does that encourage anyone who doesn’t come to the game to come to the game? I don’t think it does. “For the thousands of us who are supportive, it is important we pull together and try and pass the word around that it’s a good show out there and you can have a good time going to the football. “It’s important to support your town. It’s lovely to belong to something and have a shared experience out on a Saturday. We need everyone to take pride in the club and the town and I think that’s the way we are going to get those people fans in. “It’s dead easy for people to say we’ll never get 9,000 in, but have you invited someone along to the game? Everyone has a big part to play. “We will do our best by making he matchday experience as good as we can under the constraints we’ve got and we will try to listen to any ideas that will help. I think we have a great club going to great places. We are progressing at a sensible pace and I would like everyone to get behind us.” A walk for a good cause Chesterfield fan Ben Kirk did the unthinkable on . For Chesterfield’s opening game of the season, he completed a 60-mile walk from his very doorstep at Burntwood, Staffordshire, to the SMH Group Stadium. The Spireites won their match against Barrow with a tight 1-0 score, but the true hero was Kirk himself. He was interviewed before the kick-off and was presented to the crowd during half-time. Ben explained that he took the challenge to raise some funds for the Ashgate Hospice and Macmillan Cancer Support. What he did was more than noble, and it just goes to show what sort of fans Chesterfield has. In the interview, Kirk himself stated that anyone who wishes can also contribute to Ashgate Hospice and Macmillan Cancer Support as well. He expressed his hopes that more young people would follow in his footsteps to make the community stronger. Stadium sponsorship renewed SMH Group have been sponsoring Chesterfield’s stadium since 2023 and the professional services firm have renewed their deal with the club for another three years, meaning it will now run until the end of the 2028/29 season. Chesterfield chairman Ashley Kirk said: “We’re thrilled that SMH Group has committed to a further three years as our stadium sponsor. “Their support has been instrumental since the partnership began, and it is fantastic to continue working with a business that shares our commitment to the town and its community. “We look forward to building on this strong relationship in the seasons ahead.” Chesterfield chants After a lull in the late 2010s, the SMH Group Stadium has come to life in recent years, with performances on the pitch certainly contributing to its resurgence. Chesterfield were promoted back to the English Football League in 2024, and they reached the playoffs in their first season back. Some of the Chesterfield chants you can expect to hear at the SMH Group Stadium include: Spireite til I Die Blue Flag Flyin’ High Moliendo Cafe Just Bounce if You Love the Town Come on, You Blues Check out a video compilation of Chesterfield chants below. Best views and seating plan The SMH Group Stadium is a well-balanced, symmetrical ground, with both the sides and ends closely mirroring one another in design. For the best views of the action, you will want to sit in either the Chesterfield College Community East Stand or the LMD Vacuum Excavation West Stand, the two stands that run along the length of the pitch. While one block in the Chesterfield College Community East Stand is reserved for away supporters, the remainder of the stand is open to home fans. The most central blocks offer the clearest sightlines, so it is worth targeting seats in blocks E3-35. On the opposite side sits the LMD Vacuum Excavation Stand, widely regarded as the stadium’s main stand. Securing central seats here is slightly more complicated than in the East Stand, as the Press Box, hospitality areas and Director’s Box are all housed within it. For supporters looking to soak up the atmosphere at the SMH Group Stadium, the Motan Colortonic South Stand behind one of the goals is a great place to be. Seating plan Photo by Chesterfield Pubs for away fans at the SMH Group Stadium The main pub for away fans at Chesterfield away is the Red Lion (570 Sheffield Rd, Whittington Moor, Chesterfield S41 8LX). Alternative options nearby include: Donkey Derby (405 Sheffield Rd, Chesterfield S41 8JZ) Crown & Anchor (143 Sheffield Rd, Chesterfield S41 7JH) The Batch House (The Glass Yard, Sheffield Rd, Chesterfield S41 8JY) Food and drink at the SMH Group Stadium Fans at the SMH Group Stadium shouldn’t expect too much when it comes to food and drink, but there are some light options if you just want a quick bite to eat. A range of pies and sausage rolls are available on the concourses within the stadium, all of which are supplied to the club by a local bakery. Snacks, such as crisps and chocolate, can also be purchased. In terms of drinks, a pint of lager costs £5.50 on the concourses and soft drinks cost £3.50. Cheeseburger at Chesterfield FC ( @ChesterfieldFC ) 💷 £5.50 pic.twitter.com/HuTWhyvzkm — Footy Scran (@FootyScran) January 29, 2024 Best places to eat near the SMH Group Stadium Based on the state of the burger photographed above, it might be a better idea to grab some food away from the stadium, either before kick-off or after the full-time whistle. Some of the best restaurants in Chesterfield include: The Divan – 8 Lordsmill St, Chesterfield S41 7RW Bottle and Tyhyme – Unit 3 Elder Way, Chesterfield S40 1UN Sicily Restaurant – 78 Sheffield Rd, Chesterfield S41 7LS Getting to the SMH Group Stadium By car If you are travelling by car you will have to exit the M1 at Junction 29 and follow the A617 in the direction of Chesterfield. Continue along the dual carriageway towards the town centre, then turn right onto the A61 heading for Sheffield. At the next roundabout, take the first exit on the left and you will see the stadium on your right-hand side shortly after. Car Parking On-site parking is available at a cost of £12 per match, but spaces must be booked in advance directly through the club. Supporters who are unable to secure a space can instead park at the nearby Tesco Extra, which is located approximately 100 metres from the ground. By public transport Chesterfield Railway Station is within walking distance of the SMH Group Stadium, with the journey on foot typically taking between 20 and 30 minutes. Taxis are also readily available from the rank situated just outside the station. For those travelling by bus, head into the town centre, around a five-minute walk from the station, and catch a service from Cavendish Street. Bus journeys to the stadium usually take between five and 15 minutes, depending on traffic conditions. Disabled facilities and accessibility at SMH Group Stadium SMH Group Stadium is a fairly modern ground and, as a result, features a standard level of disabled facilities given Chesterfield’s League Two status. These features include, but are not limited to: 22 seasonal disabled parking spaces Designated wheelchair spaces in each of the four stands Raised platforms in all stands are for wheelchair users Wheelchair-friendly concourse counters Accessible toilets are located across the stadium The ground also has systems in place to help accommodate supporters with audio and/or visual impairments. For the former, there are hearing loops located within the stadium, while for the latter, Chesterfield offers a dedicated audio commentary service. SMH Group Stadium ticket prices Chesterfield tickets are available online on the club’s website or at the ticketing office. Ticket prices at SMH Group Stadium vary depending on your age and the location of your seat inside the venue. The football club lists matches on its website, for which you can book tickets, including Cup fixtures. Additionally, ticket prices extend to matchday hospitality, tailored for supporters who are willing to spend more for VIP treatment on matchdays. The following is a breakdown of Chesterfield F.C.’s matchday ticket prices for the 2026-27 season. Adults: £22-£27 66+: £20-£23 17-21: £16-“20 14-16: £14 13 and under: £10-£12 SMG Group Stadium matchday hospitality With a matchday package at Chesterfield’s stadium, you get to dine in style and have the best match viewing experience. During the 2026-27 season, supporters of Chesterfield can purchase standard VIP packages in the Haddon Suite and the SBK IT Solutions Suite at a cost of £50 for adults and £25 for U13s. The standard package offers access to a pay bar and gourmet food menu, as well as a padded seat and access to the lounge at half-time and full-time. A premium package is also available for £95 for adults and £45 for U13s. This includes a three-course meal, a padded seat, lounge access and a pay bar. SMH Group Stadium capacity The SMH Group Stadium is still relatively new, having only opened in 2010. It opened with a capacity of 10,500, and no changes have been made to the stadium since its opening date, so the capacity is still the same now. There are currently no plans to expand the stadium further, with the capacity currently meeting the demands of the club’s fan base. SMH Group Stadium tours Chesterfield put on stadium tours of the SMH Group Stadium sporadically throughout the year, typically during the summer months and school holidays. Fans are given the opportunity to take a behind-the-scenes look at the SMH Group Stadium, led by a guide who will educate them on key facts about the club’s history and traditions. On these tours, fans are taken to areas such as the Memorial Garden, the dressing rooms and the dugouts. Fans should check the club website for the latest tour dates . Prices are typically £5 per person. Nearby attractions If you are travelling a long distance to watch a match at the SMH Group Stadium, then you might want to stick around and make a weekend of the trip. After all, Chesterfield is a beautiful town with plenty of sights to see. Some of the best places in and around Chesterfield include: The crooked spire of the Parish Church of St Mary and All Saints. Harwick Old Hall Barrow Hill Roundhouse Railway Centre Queen’s Park Chesterfield Canal Concerts at the SMH Group Stadium Due to the modern nature of the stadium, it was built with more than just football in mind. As a result, it is seen as the premier concert venue in Chesterfield and has already played host to several household names. Some of the biggest artists to play at the SMH Group Stadium include: Lionel Ritchie Lionel Ritchie performed at the SMH Group Stadium in 2019 as part of his All the Hits UK Summer Tour. The ‘Dancing on the Ceiling’ hitmaker entertained fans throughout the evening, playing all of his biggest tracks. Tom Jones In the same summer that Lionel Ritchie played at the stadium, Tom Jones also played in front of a sold-out crowd at the SMH Group Stadium. The Welsh legend put on a show for the ages, playing all of his most famous songs, including Delilah and It’s Not Unusual. Elton John Elton John is the biggest artist to have played at the SMH Group Stadium. John was one of the first musical acts to perform at the stadium, with his show taking place in 2012. Chesterfield ground history Before moving to the SMH Group Stadium in 2010, the club played their home matches at Saltergate, otherwise known as the Recreation Ground. Chesterfield called the ground home from 1872, making it an emotional day when they left to move into their new home. However, the ground had passed its sell-by date, and it was demolished in 2012. SMH Group Stadium record and average attendances Record attendance At SMH Group Stadium 10,108 v Maidenhead United (National League, ) At Saltergate 30,986 v Newcastle United (Division Two, April 7th, 1949) Average attendance 2025-2026: 8,143 (League Two) 2024-2025: 8,146 (League Two) 2023-2024: 7,893 (National League) 2022-2023: 6,912 (National League) 2021-2022: 6,403 (National League) Chesterfield's local rivals Chesterfield’s biggest rivals are Mansfield Town , and the hatred between the two clubs goes beyond football. During the Miners’ Strike in the 1980s, those in Derbyshire (where Chesterfield is based) took part while those in Nottinghamshire (where Mansfield is based) didn’t. This led to those from Nottinghamshire being labelled scabs. The two sides met for the first time since 2018 at the SMH Group Stadium in an EFL Cup tie in August, with Mansfield Town coming out as 2-0 winners. The first round of the EFL Cup rarely throws up any exciting ties but the meeting between Chesterfield and Mansfield at the beginning of the 2025-26 bucked that trend, with the two long-standing foes battling it out for a spot in the second round of the competition. The visiting Stags raced into a second-minute lead away from home when Rhys Oates found the Chesterfield net in rapid time, before a second-half strike from attacker Will Evans sealed safe passage into the next stage for Mansfield. Chesterfield have failed to get one over their biggest rivals since October 2013, when the Spireites won 1-0 away at the Stags in the EFL Trophy thanks to an effort from ex-Birmingham City and Coventry City striker Gary McSheffrey. Mansfield are currently competing in League One whilst Chesterfield are a League Two outfit, meaning that there are no encounters in the pipeline between the two old foes. Ground Layout Gallery Previous Next Reviews 10th December 2019 Kevin Nash (Neutral) Chesterfield v Yeovil Town National League Tuesday 10th December 2019, 8pm Kevin Nash (Neutral) Why were you looking forward to this game and visiting the Proact Stadium? Oddly It's the second game I have been to at the Proact but was working in the area – I had been to the old Saltergate Recreation Ground to watch Reading around 98/99 and last year at the Proact to watch my local non-league team Maidenhead United. How easy was your journey/finding the ground/car parking? I followed the sat nav to my nearby hotel and only stumbled over the ground when I parked under the adjacent Tesco Superstore, I didn't actually see any signs for the ground. Before this game the rain was lashing down, the Tesco car park has an extremely small warning sign, stating you get 3 hours free parking but only 2 on a match day – I drove around to the ground and was told it was £7 to park, by this time it had stopped raining so I drove back to the hotel and walked over. It was only a 10 minute walk. What you did before the game pub/chippy etc, and were the home fans friendly? I ate beforehand at the hotel. The match was delayed but nobody knew why it turned out that it was due to a last minute pitch inspection. What you thought on seeing the ground, first impressions of away end then other sides of the Proact Stadium? The ground is new, tidy & well kept. I was not sure where Chesterfield were in the National League, however the way they are playing that could be in National League North! I paid £22 which I felt was steep and actually sat amongst the Chesterfield fans. Comment on the game itself, atmosphere, stewards, pies, facilities etc.. The game was okay. Chesterfield conceded in the first minute and that left them reeling, they went 2 – 0 down and Yeovil looked decent and in total control, they could have won by 4 or even 5. The fans were putting heat on the players, suggesting that they were not fit to wear the shirt and on Sheirdan the manager. Chesterfield looked terrible. They did get a decent consolation goal, but that was it. Comment on getting away from the ground after the game: Easy, I walked back to the hotel back in less than 10 minutes. Summary of overall thoughts of the day out: It was okay. Chesterfield look like they are serious trouble and Yeovil look good enough to go the other way and back into the Football League. See more 3rd September 2019 Michael Cromack (FC Halifax Town) Chesterfield v FC Halifax Town National League Tuesday 3rd September 2019, 7.45pm Michael Cromack (FC Halifax Town) Why were you looking forward to this game and visiting the Proact Stadium? A groundhopper and first visit. How easy was your journey/finding the ground/car parking? No far off the M1 motorway and plenty of parking around the ground. What you did before the game pub/chippy etc, and were the home fans friendly? After paying for and collecting my ticket from the ground I had enough time for a quick pint of the local poison at the Glass Works pub, which is easily visible from the stadium car park. I spoke to some home fans about my quickest route back after the game they were very helpful. What you thought on seeing the ground, first impressions of away end then other sides of the Proact Stadium? Having never been a fan of new stadiums on this occasion I will make an exception. Having only seen photos of the old Saltergate ground the opportunity of a new stadium was obviously too good for the club to turn down. Talking in the pub to a home fan the new ground was built on the site of a former glass or bottleworks (that must have been a big place). It is a very smart, tidy ground with opportunities for expansion should it be needed in the future/ Comment on the game itself, atmosphere, stewards, pies, facilities etc.. A good turn out by the away fans especially for an evening kick off. They were in fine voice before and during the match. Usual fayre at the half time interval realistically priced pies, burgers, beer etc. Stewards did a good job keeping the away fans at bay when Halifax went 3-up. Comment on getting away from the ground after the game: Not a great fan of the car to a game I normally get the train but it was a night game making the train impractical a bit of a bottleneck getting away but patience is my middle name and made it back to Yorkshire in reasonable time despite a motorway closure on the way home. Summary of overall thoughts of the day out: Another ground, an away win but had to be up at 6am the next morning for work! See more 23rd March 2019 Ross (Neutral) Chesterfield v Sutton United National League Saturday 23rd March 2019, 12:30pm Ross (Neutral) Why were you looking forward to this game and visiting the Proact Stadium? I'm in often in Sheffield so I am always looking for local games to go too and I hadn't been to the Proact Stadium yet. How easy was your journey/finding the ground/car parking? A few of us split the Uber taxi fare from Sheffield to Chesterfield, as the Proact Stadium is around a 30 minute walk from the railway station. What you did before the game pub/chippy etc, and were the home fans friendly? The Proact is one of the new 'out of town' type grounds. There is a huge Tesco store next door as well as a few fast food outlets. We didn't see any pubs so went inside the stadium for a pint and a pie. What you thought on seeing the ground, first impressions of away end then other sides of the Proact Stadium? I was very impressed. It seems that Chesterfield are too big a club not to be in the Football League and their ground represents that. Once they overcome their financial difficulties I can only see them climbing the leagues. Brand new seats and facilities, I can't fault the ground at all. Comment on the game itself, atmosphere, stewards, pies, facilities etc.. A 3-0 Chesterfield win with the big man Tom Denton playing a blinder. It was an early kick off as it was being televised by BT Sport, so the atmosphere wasn't amazing but good enough. The facilities are probably the best in the league as only a few years old. Comment on getting away from the ground after the game: We took the 30 minute walk to the train station which was easy, just long. Then a 15 minute train back into Sheffield, sp no problems at all. Summary of overall thoughts of the day out: The tickets cost £8 for Under 22's and with a pie and a pint it came to about £14. Decent football on display and a modern stadium, I can't really say a bad word See more 9th February 2019 Michael Finister-Smith (FC Halifax Town) Chesterfield v FC Halifax Town National League Saturday 9th February 2019, 3pm Michael Finister-Smith (FC Halifax Town) Why were you looking forward to this game and visiting the Proact Stadium? Having fond memories of many visits to Saltergate in the past, I was looking forward to my first visit to their new stadium. It was also a match I thought we should win, but I should have known better. How easy was your journey/finding the ground/car parking? I was driving and it is an easy run not too far off the M1. I decided to park at the ground and pay the extortionate £5 charge but as others have posted, there is plenty of parking elsewhere within walking distance. What you did before the game pub/chippy etc, and were the home fans friendly? I was going to go to the Derby Donkey pub just up from the ground but it looked like one of those boring chain food chains, so I went instead to the Glasshouse right opposite the ground. It was quite busy but there was a wide range of real ales and it was a good choice of venue. There was a bouncer on the door but there was no trouble and it was a friendly and welcoming pub with fans of both teams chatting. What you thought on seeing the ground, first impressions of away end then other sides of the Proact Stadium? It is a very impressive ground for our league. There was a good view of the pitch and there was a refreshment area selling food and alcohol to those who wanted it. I had a steak pie which was delicious. Comment on the game itself, atmosphere, stewards, pies, facilities etc.. The game was disappointing and we lost to a dubious penalty. However more frustrating is that we barely had a shot on goal. What was terrible is that some idiot had smuggled in a flare which he set off in the away end, causing mayhem and I left feeling even more depressed than with the match. Hopefully, they will be caught and banned. Comment on getting away from the ground after the game: It was very easy to get out considering there were over 4000 attending. Match Details: Fixture: Crawley Town vs Grimsby Town Venue: Broadfield Stadium Turnstiles Open: Approximately 60 minutes before kick-off Kit Colour: The Mariners will be wearing our Cream Third Kit for this fixture. Ticket Information: Tickets can be purchased on the day via card payments only. Adult Seating (East Stand) – £22 Standing (North Stand) – £20 Over 60 / Student (with ID) Seating (East Stand) – £17 Standing (North Stand) – £15 Youth (14–20) Seating/Standing – £10 Under 14 Seating/Standing – £2 Carer Free with an ambulance disabled ticket. Away Supporters: Town supporters will be located in the East Stand for seating and the North Stand for standing. Both areas are covered, with the standing section located behind the goal and seating situated in the side stand. Getting to the Ground: Postcode: RH11 9RX By Car From the M25, take the M23 towards Gatwick Airport/Brighton. Leave the M23 at Junction 11 (A264 Horsham). At the roundabout turn right onto the A23 towards Crawley. The stadium is on the left just before the next roundabout. Parking: Parking at the stadium is for permit and season ticket holders only. Supporters are advised to use Broadfield Business Park (RH11 9RT) or Brighton Road, both of which offer free parking and are a short walk from the ground. Disabled Supporters: There are three spaces available for disabled away supporters at the stadium. Parking is free for blue badge holders, which must be displayed. To book, please contact: tickets@crawleytownfc.com By Train: The nearest station is Crawley, which is approximately one mile from the stadium. The walk takes around 20-25 minutes, while taxis are available outside the station. Alternatively, the Fastway 10 bus from Stop A drops supporters outside the ground. Food & Drink: There is limited food provision immediately around the stadium, although Tesco Express on Downland Drive (RH11 8SW) is located around a five-minute walk away. Inside the stadium, Crawley Town operate an away fanzone located next to the away turnstiles at the North end, serving alcohol as well as hot and soft drinks. A number of catering trucks are also located near Redz Bar and the ticket office. Cash Machines: The nearest cash machine is located at Tesco Express, approximately a five-minute walk from the ground. Programme: Crawley Town no longer produce an official matchday programme. However, a supporter-produced publication titled “The Red Devils Diary” will be available priced at £2. Flags: Flags are permitted but must not be on poles and must be securely tied. Supporters should speak to a steward on arrival who will assist with placement. Recommended Pubs for Away Fans: Redz Bar at the stadium will be welcoming away supporters for this fixture. Other pubs that welcome away fans include: Jubilee Oak (Wetherspoons) – RH10 1BA (Town Centre) Railway Pub – Brighton Road, RH10 6AA New Moon Pub – Brighton Road, RH10 6SZ Please note The Downman Pub is for home supporters only. Mariners Respects: We’re proud of the outstanding support Grimsby Town receives both home and away. We want everyone attending to enjoy the match in a welcoming environment. Abusive, indecent, or discriminatory behaviour, including racist, homophobic, sexist, sectarian, xenophobic, or anti-disability actions, will not be tolerated. The Club may issue bans, including indefinite bans, to anyone engaging in such behaviour. We look forward to seeing the Mariners backed loudly and proudly at the Broadfield Stadium. Safe travels to all supporters making the journey. All the important information travelling supporters need to know is included in Kristine Green’s Away Travel Guide! What colour kit are we wearing? We will be in our all-blue away kit for this match. What’s the ticket information? There is an away ticket office open from 12pm next to the away turnstiles for fans to purchase on the day by cash or card. Any collections will also be left here but won’t be available until around 1.30pm. Ticket prices are as follows: Adult – £25 Senior Citizens – £19 12-16 years old – £12.50 Under 11 – £7.50 Disabled – £19 What stand are Town fans in? Town fans are in the Whitby Morrison Ice Cream Van Stand – this is an all seater covered side that runs the length of the pitch. How do I get to the ground? Post Code is CW2 6EB. Exit the M6 and follow signs for Crewe A500 and then A5020. Take the 3 rd exit on the roundabout, at the next one take the first exit signposted Crewe Town Centre and Railway Station. Go past Crewe Hall on the right and then continue onto Weston Road. Continue over the next roundabout and then left at the one after that and past the train station. Then take the 2 nd left onto Gresty Road and the stadium will be on your left. Where is the best place to park? There is a large 564 space car park at the rear of the Main Stand – it’s first come first served and charges £3.50. There is some parking on the industrial estate on Weston Road – which is about a 10 minute walk to the ground. There is some street parking but be mindful of how you park. Information for disabled fans travelling? Blue badge parking is available at the public car park outside of the ground. This is first come, first served and a blue badge must be on display. When do turnstiles open? Turnstiles open at 2pm. What is the nearest train station to the stadium and what is the approximate distance and walking time? Crewe train station is only 5 minutes away. Turn left out of the station and then take the 2 nd left, which is Gresty Road. The stadium is a short walk down this road. Recommended pubs for away fans? There are no specific pubs for away fans so plenty to choose from. A couple specifically mentioned are: The Corner Bar at the Royal Hotel, The Cheshire Inn and The Brunswick – all located on Nantwich Road – 5 minute walk. Food available in the area? There are food places on Nantwich Road and a chippy opposite the home ticket office called Bennies. Where is the nearest cash machine to the Stadium? There’s a cash machine at the train station or on Nantwich Road – both are about a 5 minute walk away. What food and drink is available in the stadium? Inside the ground you have the usual burgers, pies and hot/cold drinks. Alcohol is available. Both cash and card is accepted. What is the process for supporters looking to bring flags into the stadium? Flags larger than 250cm at their widest or longest section are not permitted. Stewards will advise the best place for flags to be hung. Is a programme available? Crewe no longer have a printed matchday programme. We’re looking forward to seeing our supporters cheering on the lads at Gresty Road! Tickets Supporters have been given an initial allocation of 400 tickets in the seated section, with a further 700 tickets available in the standing section if required. https://tothe92.co.uk/groundguide/gillin.text: HOME GROUND GUIDES PREMIER LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP LEAGUE ONE LEAGUE TWO INTERNATIONAL OTHERS PANORAMIC PHOTOS PREMIER LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP LEAGUE ONE LEAGUE TWO INTERNATIONAL OTHERS CONTACT Home League Two Guide Gillingham Gillingham FC - MEMS Priestfield Stadium Stadium Info Priestfield Stadium underwent extensive redevelopment during the late 1990s, which brought the capacity down from nearly 20,000 to a current figure of 11,582. All stands have been re-constructed since 1997, although one is still only of a temporary uncovered nature. This houses the away fans. The Medway Stand runs alongside the pitch and offers a fantastic view of the action from all areas, as does the Rainham End behind the goal. The Gordon Road stand running parallel to the Medway Stand, was the first to be redeveloped and comes complete with approximately 8 pillars, all arranged to block your view, if you're toward the back, of at least one of the goals. A new fan zone has opened at the back of the Rainham End and is open 2 hours before kick off. Away Fans Visiting supporters are housed in the Brian Moore stand behind one of the goals. The stand is temporary and without a roof although of quite a decent size. It's cold and wet during the winter so don't forget your coats. The view from this stand is quite impressive at this level with 3 relatively new builds to peruse. 200 covered seats are made available to visiting fans in the Gordon Road Stand. Visiting fans enter via the turnstiles on Gordon Road. Stadium Layout Priestfield Stadium seating plan: Best Places To Sit For a detailed look into the best and worst places to sit at Gillingham's Priestfield Stadium, check out their team page on 'Where To Sit?' which features plenty of information and photos submitted by fans with views from their seats - Best Places To Sit at Priestfield Stadium Where To Drink In the town centre, the Will Adams pub offers a good place for both home and away fans to mix. It offers a lot of friendly banter and a pint while you're at it. Also recommended is the Fleur de Lis at 46 Gillingham Road as an away fans pub. Elsewhere, fans can try The Cricketers at 40 Sturdee Avenue and The Napier Arms at 153 Britton Street. There are plenty of restaurants and takeaways to choose from in the town centre with a pretty decent selection located on the High Street if you fancy something a little more substantial to eat. The Eel Pie Island cafe which can be found on the right as you walk through the high street away from the ground is a particularly popular place before the game and serves a mean double pie and mash with gravy! Parking There are extensive residents’ permit restrictions on roads immediately surrounding Priestfield Stadium. Supporters should check restrictions carefully and avoid assuming that spaces are available for matchday parking. A good place to head for is the car park at the scout hall on Ingram Road (ME7 1YL). It's approximately £5 to park and conveniently located between the town centre and the stadium. Secure a parking space near to Priestfield Stadium and save £££. Simply book a nearby space or driveway with JustPark Directions Get directions to the Priestfield Stadium from your house by entering your post code or location below: By Train The nearest / closest train station to Gillingham's Priestfield Stadium is Gillingham and is served by High Speed Javelin trains from London St Pancras International (25 and 55 minutes past every hour) and London Victoria (22 and 52 minutes past every hour). There are a number of slow speed trains that also serve the station from both of these and 2 further from Charing Cross at 9 and 39 minutes past every hour on Saturdays. Simon Chaplin tells me: A return will set you back approximately £15 although on the South Eastern line you can use Groupsave where 4 people can travel for the price of two provided they all travel together. From the station, the walk up to Priestfield will take around 10 minutes. From the station, turn left into Balmoral Road. When you reach the end of the road and come to a crossroads (ignoring the T-Junction which doesn't count!) you will see a road straight ahead of you - Priestfield Road. The ground is situated at the top of this road with the visitors turnstiles at the far end. Ultimate How to Get To Gillingham FC Guide For an in depth look at how to get to Gillingham's Priestfield Stadium by car or by train, parking advice, accessibility information as well as shuttle buses and park and ride details, check out the link below! Ultimate How to Get To Gillingham FC's Priestfield Stadium Guide The Games To See Rivals - Charlton, Millwall, Swindon Priestfield Stadium FAQ Where do away fans usually sit at Priestfield Stadium? Away supporters are usually accommodated in the Brian Moore Stand behind one of the goals. The arrangement can change depending on the game, so supporters should check the details for their specific fixture before travelling. What is the nearest train station to Priestfield Stadium? Gillingham railway station is the nearest station and the stadium is within walking distance. Can you park at Priestfield Stadium? Parking immediately around the stadium is limited because Priestfield is surrounded by residential streets, so train travel is often more convenient. Is the away end at Gillingham covered? The Brian Moore Stand has historically been an uncovered temporary-style stand, so visiting supporters should check current matchday information and the weather forecast before travelling. Is Priestfield close to Gillingham town centre? Yes, the stadium is within walking distance of Gillingham town centre and railway station. How long have Gillingham played at Priestfield? Gillingham have played at Priestfield since the club's early history in the nineteenth century. Is Priestfield Stadium accessible? Accessible facilities and viewing arrangements are available for disabled supporters. Is Gillingham the only current EFL club based in Kent? Gillingham are historically the county's most established Football League club, although league membership of clubs can change between seasons. FANS REVIEWS David Crossfield, 9th February 2019 - Gillingham v Barnsley Travel: I travelled down to Kings Cross by train from Doncaster using Hull Trains, which was the cheapest. The buffet had an excellent bottle of Newsome ale on sale. The train was late so I missed my planned connection from St. Pancras. There is a half hourly service which takes 45 minutes. Refreshments: I met my friend in Rochester, which is two stops and 7 minutes from Gillingham on the train. He had been in a Wetherspoons and saw a few Barnsley fans in there. I know some coaches stopped off at Gravesend. We went to the Coopers Arms, a fantastic old pub which serves several real ales. We were the only football fans in there as most use pubs on the High Street. As I was late, we didn't get a chance to visit any more Rochester pubs, unfortunately. We got a train at about 2 pm to Gillingham to visit the Past and Present micropub. It's the opposite direction from the ground as you leave the train station, but worth finding if you like real ale. There was a good mix of home and away fans and friendly service. We set off for the ground about 2.40 pm and arrived just in time for kick off. Impressions: The open away end is okay if it's not raining, but it seems strange walking under the scaffolding to access your seat. The other three sides of the ground look fine for League 1. Some Barnsley fans were in a small seated area to our right. These were only available to families, disabled and older fans. Atmosphere: The stewarding was unobtrusive. As usual, we were patted down outside. Barnsley took 800 fans, which I thought was a bit disappointing, but over 1500 had bought tickets for the following away trip to Portsmouth, so they were obviously choosing games. Barnsley scored straight from the kick off. 15 seconds to be exact! By half time it was 2-0 and should have been more. It wasn't easy to see the action at the far end of the ground. It seemed a long way off, but I'm used to watching from the halfway line. Barnsley made it 3-0 in the second half before the Gills pulled one back. Barnsley striker Keiffer Moore clashed heads accidentally with a Gills defender and was stretchered off after a 12 minute delay. Barnsley made it 1-4 in the 101st minute. It's suggested that meant they had scored the earliest and latest away goals in the club's history. The Reds fans were jubilant. Gill's fans were understandably subdued. I rarely have refreshments in the ground so I can't comment. The toilet facilities were adequate for the number of away fans. Exit: It was an easy ten-minute walk to the train station for the 17.21 back to St.Pancras. Enjoy: A good day out. Obviously, the result helped, but the injury to Keiffer Moore did take the shine off it. The journey was fine and not too long. Rochester looked good with the Castle and Cathedral. https://gtfc.co.uk/northampton-town-trav.text: News Club News Ticket News Youth & Academy Women’s Team Teams Men’s First Team Fixtures and Results Women’s Team Youth Team Tickets Buy Tickets 26/27 Season Tickets 1878 Club Memberships Shop Club Shop Subscribe To The Mariner Mascot Packages Silent Auctions Mariners TV About Visitors & Fans Matchdays Grimsby Town Foundation Latest Accounts Opening Hours Matchday Accreditation Who’s Who at GTFC Ground Regulations Club Policies SafeGaurding Vacancies Club Ownership Academy Player Care Fallen Mariners Reporting Discrimination Commercial Match Sponsorships Matchday Hospitality Advertising Memberships Half Time Bonanza Mariners Lottery X-twitter Instagram Facebook-square Youtube Northampton Town Travel Guide News Club News Ticket News Youth & Academy Women’s Team Teams Men’s First Team Fixtures and Results Women’s Team Youth Team Tickets Buy Tickets 26/27 Season Tickets 1878 Club Memberships Shop Club Shop Subscribe To The Mariner Mascot Packages Silent Auctions Mariners TV About Visitors & Fans Matchdays Grimsby Town Foundation Latest Accounts Opening Hours Matchday Accreditation Who’s Who at GTFC Ground Regulations Club Policies SafeGaurding Vacancies Club Ownership Academy Player Care Fallen Mariners Reporting Discrimination Commercial Match Sponsorships Matchday Hospitality Advertising Memberships Half Time Bonanza Mariners Lottery Club News , Match Previews February 17, 2023 Ahead of tomorrow’s trip to take on Northampton Town at Sixfields, Kristine Green’s Away Day Travel Guide has all the important information supporters need… What colour kit are we in for this game? We’re in blue for this game. What’s the ticket information? Tickets can be purchased on the day via the small ticket booth near the turnstiles. This is card or contactless only. Prices below are the increased prices for on the day purchases. Adults – £24 Over 65 – £20 Under 18 – £12 U7 – Free Disabled – As above category plus a free carer How do I get to the ground? Post Code is NN5 5QA – with Northampton Saints at home, and with a large crowd expected, please allow extra time to arrive and find parking. From the North leave the M1 at junction 16, take the A45 towards Northampton and the ground is on the right. From the South leave the M1 at junction 15a, take the A43 towards Northampton and the ground is on the right. What stand are we in? Town fans are in the South Stand which is a seated, covered stand. Northampton Town operate on an allocated seat basis and request that fans use the seat number shown on their ticket. When do turnstiles open? Turnstiles open around 90 minutes before kick-off. Where is the best place to park? There is a good sized car park at the ground which costs £4, It can get full quickly and is slow to empty. Do not park on any of the retail parks as fines are issued. Is there disabled parking? Disabled parking spaces are pre-booked via 01604 683777 and allocated on a first come, first served basis. You cannot book these spaces on the day. What is the nearest train station to the stadium and what is the approximate distance and walking time? Northampton station is a good two miles away so a taxi is your best bet but the area will be busy due to the rugby too. Otherwise, it’s a thirty-minute or so walk to the ground. Recommended pubs for away fans? The ground itself has a supporters bar which welcomes away fans or there is the Walter Tull on the retail park as well as numerous pubs in town but this is a forty-minute walk away. Just outside of town, on the A45, is the Red Lion Truck Stop (NN7 4DE) which is a bar/restaurant with sport on TVs. Food available in the area? There are a number of chain restaurants including KFC, TGI Friday’s and McDonalds as well as a Hungry Horse pub. Where is the nearest cash machine to the Stadium? Both the BP petrol station and Sainsbury’s on the retail park have free to use cash machines. What food and drink is available on the concourse at the stadium? Both hot and cold food and drink items are available inside the ground. There is a bar available in the away end which accepts both cash and card. What is the process for supporters looking to bring flags/drums into the stadium? There are generally no issues with supporters bringing flags but they must be displayed in a safe manner, not blocking walkways. Stewards will be on hand to assist where needed. No drums are permitted in the ground. Is a programme available? A programme is available on the day, costing £3.00. https://v2.shrewsburytown.com/news/2026/.text: Skip to main content Latest News Buy Tickets STFC Matches STFC Events STFC Watch STFC Shop STFC Our Club STFC Teams STFC Foundation STFC Contact Us RETRO Register / Log in RETRO Competitive football is back - with Salop making the trip to Greater Manchester to take on Salford City in the first round of the Carabao Cup tomorrow. We've put together everything you need to know ahead of Saturday's clash. From getting to the stadium to nearby pubs, parking, food, and ground information. Whether you're making the trip for the first time or you're a regular on the road, you'll find all the key information you need here. Ticket Prices: Seating: Adults: £15 Seniors: £9 Under-22s: £9 Terrace: Adults: £12 Seniors: £7 Under-22s: £7 Tickets Card Payment at Turnstile A2 will be available for the East Stand Terrace on the day of the game. (£1 increase on matchday). Admission for all away supporters is via Turnstile A situated at the East end of the ground on Moor Lane. Travel: Supporters travelling by car should be aware that there is no dedicated away supporter parking at the stadium, with many surrounding roads operating a residents' parking scheme on matchdays. There are streets available with no restrictions outside of the restricted parking zone. There is a large car park at the Whitefield Park & Ride (M45 8AB), where you can catch bus 95 or 98, which both run near to the stadium. For Salopians travelling by train, the closest train station to the AIG Stadium is Manchester Victoria, with the quickest route to Saturday's venue being via public transport, with taxis being available from the station alongside the number 97 & 98 bus, which stop by the stadium. Away end: Salop fans will be situated in the East Stand terrace, with a portion of seated tickets available in the North Stand, located on Moor Lane. Same-level access is available at the away entrance for travelling Town fans, as well as accessible toilets situated in the away fan zone. Supporters will have the choice of two kiosk's is the away fanzone; Babs' Cafe offers a range of food and drink, including Burgers, Hot Dogs, Pies, Soft Drinks, Hot Drinks and more. There is also a kiosk next door that serves a range of alcoholic drinks, pies and confectionery. There are no pubs in the immediate vicinity of the ground, and the surrounding area is largely residential; however, the Fairways Lodge is available ten minutes away. A bit further, you'll find the Friendship Inn on Scholes Lane, which is about a 15-20 minute walk to the ground. Kit: Town will line up for the first time competitively in this year's new navy home shirt with white shorts, with the goalkeepers repping the Purple away shirt on the road for the first time in competitive action, avoiding a clash with the hosts' recently revealed Tangerine home strip. Where to watch: For supporters unable to join us in Salford, the game will be shown live on Sky Sports+. Audio commentary will be available through the club website via the recently launched match commentary service. Launched alongside StreamAMG. https://gtfc.co.uk/away-day-guide-tranme.text: News Club News Ticket News Youth & Academy Women’s Team Teams Men’s First Team Fixtures and Results Women’s Team Youth Team Tickets Buy Tickets 26/27 Season Tickets 1878 Club Memberships Shop Club Shop Subscribe To The Mariner Mascot Packages Silent Auctions Mariners TV About Visitors & Fans Matchdays Grimsby Town Foundation Latest Accounts Opening Hours Matchday Accreditation Who’s Who at GTFC Ground Regulations Club Policies SafeGaurding Vacancies Club Ownership Academy Player Care Fallen Mariners Reporting Discrimination Commercial Match Sponsorships Matchday Hospitality Advertising Memberships Half Time Bonanza Mariners Lottery X-twitter Instagram Facebook-square Youtube Away Day Guide – Tranmere Rovers News Club News Ticket News Youth & Academy Women’s Team Teams Men’s First Team Fixtures and Results Women’s Team Youth Team Tickets Buy Tickets 26/27 Season Tickets 1878 Club Memberships Shop Club Shop Subscribe To The Mariner Mascot Packages Silent Auctions Mariners TV About Visitors & Fans Matchdays Grimsby Town Foundation Latest Accounts Opening Hours Matchday Accreditation Who’s Who at GTFC Ground Regulations Club Policies SafeGaurding Vacancies Club Ownership Academy Player Care Fallen Mariners Reporting Discrimination Commercial Match Sponsorships Matchday Hospitality Advertising Memberships Half Time Bonanza Mariners Lottery Club News October 6, 2023 Ahead of tomorrow’s trip to take on Tranmere Rovers, our Away Day Guide includes all the key information supporters making the journey need… What kit are we in for this game? We’re in our red away kit for this game. What’s the ticket information? Tickets are available on the day from the Club Shop located at Prenton Park from 1.30pm. They are priced as follows: Adults – £25.00 Over 65’s – £20.00 Young Person – £18.00 Under 18’s – £11.00 Under 12’s – £7.00 Disabled and PA – £18.00 or age-related price and carer free of charge. How do I get to the ground? The postcode for Prenton Park is CH42 9PY. From the M6/M56, use the M53 and then exit at junction 4 onto the B5151 from the fourth exit of the roundabout. The ground is signposted from here. After two and a half miles, Mount Road leads onto Storeton Road – turn right at the traffic lights near the church onto Prenton Road West. The round is further down on the right. What stand are we in? Town fans are in the Cowshed Stand – this is a covered all-seater stand behind the goal. When do turnstiles open? Turnstiles open at 1.30pm. Where is the best place to park? Parking at the ground is now fully booked. There is street parking but just be mindful of resident restrictions and road closures an hour before kick-off and 30 minutes after the end of the game. The Mersey Clipper pub next door does have a small car park but this will fill early on. Parking for disabled supporters? There are a limited number of accessible spaces available at the ground. They are prioritised to those with blue badges. What is the nearest train station to the stadium and what is the approximate distance and walking time? Both Birkenhead Central and Rock Ferry Station around a mile away. Recommended pubs for away fans? The Mersey Clipper welcomes small groups. Prenton Park and Halfway House are also options and there is a fanzone in the main car park of the ground. Food available in the area? There is a deli and a chippy which is quite good near the ground. There is also a Tesco Express down the road. Borough Road also has other takeaways. The fan park at the ground will welcome fans and is serving both food and drink from 12pm. Where is the nearest cash machine to the Stadium? Tesco Express has a free-to-use cash machine near the away end on Borough Road. What food and drink is available on the concourse at the stadium? Both cash and card are accepted. The away end has hot and cold drinks as well as burgers and pies. They also have snacks for junior fans. Alcohol is also served in the way end. What is the process for supporters looking to bring flags into the stadium? Flags must have safety certificates – stewards will advise where to place. What’s the ticket information? Tickets are available to purchase on the day from the North Stand ticket booth (which opens from 1pm) at the following prices: Adult £12.00 65 & over £ 7.00 12-16 years £ 5.00 Student £ 5.00 Under 11 Free with adult Please note that advance sales from Blundell Park end at 3pm today. How do I get to the ground? Postcode for the ground is YO32 9AE. It is advised to follow the guidance in the ‘Where’s best place to park’ section rather than drive to the stadium. What stand are we in? We’re located in the ‘West Stand’ which is along the side of the pitch. Where is the best place to park? There’s plenty of parking in the city centre, where you can catch a shuttle bus to the ground or you can use the park and ride. The Y22 shuttle bus between Stonebow and the LNER Community Stadium is available. If you’re looking to use this, you need to purchase from the First Bus app – Adults £3.50 return and child/concession £2 return. There is a dedicated area with the Monks Cross park and ride for 400 cars. Tickets must be purchased in advance from here. The service runs every 12 minutes before and after the game. Parking for disabled supporters? Any supporters required disabled parking need to call the home ticket office on 01904 950950. What is the nearest train station to the stadium and what is the approximate distance and walking time? York station is around 3 miles away from the stadium so a taxi or bus to the ground is likely needed! Recommended pubs for away fans? No designated pubs so take your pick! The most popular are: Postern Gate (Wetherspoons) – YO1 9NX The Punch Bowl (Wetherspoons) – YO1 8AN Yates – YO1 9QT Slug and Lettuce – YO1 8AD There are no ‘traditional’ pubs near the ground. The only places in the area are Hollywood Bowl and Vallado Lounge, which serves food. Food available in the area? There is a range of places to eat within the city centre itself. But near to the ground you have chain outlets such as Nandos, Prezzo, Estabulo and Costa Coffee. Where is the nearest cash machine to the Stadium? There’s a cash machine at Sainsburys across from the retail park. What food and drink is available on the concourse at the stadium? The usual burgers, pies and hot dogs are available along with hot/cold drinks and alcohol. What is the process for supporters looking to bring flags into the stadium? Flags are allowed but must be placed following stewards instructions. What kit are we in for this game? We will be wearing our home kit of black and white striped shirts, black shorts and white socks.
